security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel IOPMP driver, during the atomic rule-update sequence (MDSTALL write → poll is_busy → update settings → MDSTALL resume), if the driver or concurrent code writes to ERR_CFG.stall_violation_en within Steps 1-3 of the programming sequence, the hardware behavior becomes undefined per spec. This means a transaction may be checked against a partially-updated rule set, violating the atomicity guarantee that every transaction is checked either entirely before or entirely after the update.
security_spec.summary: Writing ERR_CFG.stall_violation_en during the IOPMP atomic programming sequence (Steps 1-3) yields undefined behavior, potentially allowing DMA transactions to bypass IOPMP enforcement by being checked against incomplete rule sets.

findings.finding: These are clock gate definitions providing peripheral clocks (pclk/aclk) to the IOPMP hardware block on the T-Head TH1520 SoC. They do not touch any IOPMP control registers (ERR_CFG, MDSTALL, etc.) — they are purely clock infrastructure with no security implication for the spec's atomic rule-update concern.
